mainEvent.title: Tue 11/17 · Nvidia reports, its first quarter without Huang
mainEvent.body: Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close (results about 4:20p, call 5:00p) with interim CEO Colette Kress on the call. The Street expects non-GAAP EPS of about **$2.47–2.49** on revenue near **$109B** (guidance $108B ±2%) and wants a January-quarter outlook around $125B; options imply an 8–9% move. The stock fell 13% last week after Jensen Huang resigned. It is a packed week: October retail sales Tuesday 8:30a, Fed minutes Wednesday 2:00p, Walmart Thursday before the open, and Anthropic's record IPO is expected to start trading Thursday.

stories.title: Nvidia reports Tuesday under a cloud.
stories.body: Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 after Tuesday's close, its first quarter since Jensen Huang resigned Thursday; interim CEO Colette Kress leads the call. Consensus is about $2.47–2.49 non-GAAP EPS on roughly $109B of revenue against guidance of $108B ±2%, and analysts want a January-quarter outlook near $125B. On Fox News Sunday Morning Futures, Treasury Secretary Bessent said he wants answers within 10 days on whether Nvidia used shell companies to sell top chips to China ("Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese"). The FT reports Nvidia approached Arm CEO Rene Haas; Nvidia calls candidate talk premature. NVDA fell 13% last week to $162.85.

stories.title: Anthropic's record IPO is set to debut Thursday.
stories.body: Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday night and start trading on Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT. It is selling 825 million shares at $70–78, up to about $64.4B, plus a $26B concurrent private placement (Nvidia and Google about $10B each), at a valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion; the book is reported about six times oversubscribed. It would be the largest listing ever. Polymarket prices a listing by Nov 19 at about 93%.

stories.title: Warsh, retail sales and Fed minutes test the hike case.
stories.body: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Monday at noon, October retail sales land Tuesday at 8:30a (about +0.2% expected after +0.8%), and Wednesday's 2:00p minutes cover the Oct 27–28 meeting, where the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% with two members favoring a hike. More than a dozen Fed speeches fill the week. After last week's hot CPI and a 10-year that ended near 5.15%, prediction markets price a 25bp hike on Dec 9 at about 87–89% and a bigger move at about 11%.

stories.title: Weekend Gulf flare-up; oil opens flat.
stories.body: Bahrain said Sunday its air defenses intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks, its first since September; the IRGC claimed six drones at a US radar site, with no damage confirmed. Iran's navy says tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, which Reuters could not verify and the US military disputes. Oil barely reacted: WTI was about $88.50 (−0.1%) at 6:28p Sunday after settling at $88.56 Friday; Brent settled at $95.84, a second weekly loss, as the IEA sees a supply surplus this quarter.

stories.title: Retailers report into the holiday season.
stories.body: Home Depot (est. about $3.84–3.87 EPS) and Disney report Tuesday morning; Lowe's (about $2.86–2.89), TJX ($1.33) and Target (about $2.03–2.07) Wednesday; Walmart Thursday at 7:00a (about $0.63–0.64 on roughly $187B, guided $0.62–0.64), with Ross, Gap and Intuit after Thursday's close and BJ's Friday. Polymarket gives Disney about 94% to beat $1.69 and Home Depot about 46% to beat $3.95. Tuesday's retail sales set the tone.

stories.title: Airlines dig out after the nationwide ground stop.
stories.body: Friday's FAA ground stop on all departing US flights lasted about five hours; FlightAware counted 9,159 cancellations Friday and more than 3,800 Saturday. A preliminary FAA review blamed overloaded old routers on the air traffic control network, and Homeland Security said there was no sign of a cyberattack. Airspace was operating normally by Saturday morning, though Transportation Secretary Duffy warned of more disruption as crews reposition and asked Congress for emergency modernization funds. Airline stocks slipped into Friday's close.
